official_measurement_examples.name: European protected species status
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natterjack toads are a European protected species; killing, injury, disturbance, spawn taking and damage to breeding or resting places are protected activities.

official_measurement_examples.name: Absence-record limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England standing advice explicitly says absence of a record does not mean natterjack toads are absent because survey data may not exist for the location.

official_measurement_examples.name: Survey timing distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's general protected-species timetable identifies April to May for aquatic natterjack surveys and July to September for terrestrial surveys, subject to conditions.

official_measurement_examples.name: A44 mitigation trigger
official_measurement_examples.fact: A44 is required where work would otherwise unlawfully affect natterjack toads, their breeding or resting places or access to shelter.

official_measurement_examples.name: A44 evidence pack
official_measurement_examples.fact: An A44 application requires a method statement, a reasoned statement and suitable ecological references in the circumstances stated by Natural England.

official_measurement_examples.name: A44 decision period
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England states it will decide whether to issue an A44 licence within 30 working days of receiving the application.

official_measurement_examples.name: LR13 reporting duty
official_measurement_examples.fact: Actions under a natterjack mitigation licence use the LR13 European protected species report route and the report is due no later than two weeks after licence expiry even when no action was taken.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natterjack survey, mitigation licensing and reporting do not themselves establish planning permission, species absence, land ownership or parcel development capacity.

core_rules: natterjack-toad protection law is not proof toads are present on a parcel
natterjack survey result is not planning permission
planning permission is not an A44 mitigation licence
A44 mitigation licence is distinct from A29 survey or research authority
absence of a biodiversity record is not proof of species absence
survey evidence must retain its season date methods and spatial scope
aquatic and terrestrial survey windows must not be merged into a year-round clearance claim
reasoned statement is licence-application evidence not a planning grant
LR13 reporting compliance is not evidence of species absence
historic licence completion is not current parcel clearance
natterjack protection does not determine land ownership
licensing does not reserve development capacity
mitigation compliance does not create access rights
planning standing advice is not a planning decision
no parcel natterjack clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
